prompts.text: When did keeping the peace begin to cost you your own peace?
Tell me about somebody who respected a truth you struggled to admit.
What part of being understood feels harder than being liked?
An easy agreement sometimes hides an unspoken disagreement. When have you noticed this between people?
Be remembered for comforting someone or for helping them face an uncomfortable truth?
Which relationship changed how you define responsibility towards another person?
Someone misses the version of you who never objected. How would you explain your growth?
An explanation does not automatically create an obligation to forgive. Where do you draw the distinction?
What do you lose when you always present yourself as the capable person?
Describe a time someone stayed curious about you after your views changed.
Which expectation have you mistaken for a promise in a relationship?
What helps you recognise a connection built on mutual choice rather than convenience?
Being needed sometimes disguises a wish to feel valued. How do you recognise the difference in yourself?
A person apologises sincerely but keeps asking when everything will feel normal. What would you want them to understand?
When has distance given you a fairer view of somebody?
Receive a difficult truth early or discover it later with an explanation for the delay?
Tell me about a relationship which improved when you stopped trying to be impressive.
Which part of closeness do you find easiest to give and hardest to receive?
Loyalty loses its meaning when it requires pretending harm never happened. What does honest loyalty involve?
What do you want people to understand about the way you withdraw?
Somebody says, 'I did it for you,' about a choice you never requested. How would you respond?
What has another person's disappointment taught you about limits you need to keep?
Describe a moment when you felt respected despite hearing an answer you disliked.
People sometimes grieve a possibility rather than a relationship they experienced. Have you recognised this feeling?
When does understanding someone's background help you, and when does it become an excuse for them?
What would change if you stopped treating every misunderstanding as proof of rejection?
Trust somebody's clear limits or their willingness to agree to almost anything?
A relationship feels easier because you have stopped mentioning what bothers you. What would you examine first?
Who helped you see a need you had learnt to minimise?
Tell me about a goodbye which felt caring even though it hurt.
History gives a relationship context, not unlimited permission. How do you decide what history should count for?
What do you notice in yourself when another person succeeds at something you want?
A person might forgive a mistake while losing confidence in a promise. What helps you distinguish those responses?
When have you confused being familiar with being safe?
Someone asks you to mediate an argument, but you care about both people. What would fair involvement look like?
Describe a time listening changed what you thought someone owed you.
Which relationship revealed a habit you had defended as part of your personality?
Ask someone to explain their intention or explain the effect their words had on you first?
What does receiving care without earning it bring up for you?
A peaceful ending sometimes requires accepting an incomplete explanation. How do you feel about unfinished answers?
Someone praises you for a sacrifice you now regret. How would you speak honestly about it?
What have you learnt from a relationship in which affection and compatibility differed?
Tell me about somebody who admitted they had misunderstood you without asking you to comfort them.
When do you feel responsible for managing another person's emotions?
A relationship's public story sometimes leaves little room for its private reality. What makes honest conversation possible then?
Which kind of disappointment tempts you to become less generous?
A person wants reassurance you do not honestly feel able to give. What would a kind answer sound like?
Have your effort recognised or have your needs understood without explaining the effort?
Describe a time you changed a relationship by changing your own response rather than persuading the other person.
What would respectful disagreement require you to tolerate emotionally?
Consistency matters most when keeping a promise becomes inconvenient. Which promises have taught you this?
What do you wish you had known before becoming someone's main source of support?
When has someone's confidence in you felt like pressure rather than encouragement?
You sometimes notice a relationship's imbalance only after you need help. What changed your understanding of reciprocity?
A person returns with changed behaviour but no acknowledgment of the past. What would you need to discuss?
Tell me about a time you felt cared for without feeling watched or managed.
What makes an apology feel like an invitation to repair rather than a request to stop talking?
Resolve a disagreement with full agreement or with a clear plan for living with the difference?
Which of your needs becomes harder to express when you admire someone?
The person who notices a problem first does not automatically own the job of solving it. Where have you seen this expectation?
When does patience become a way of postponing a decision you already understand?
Two people care equally but expect very different levels of contact. What should they clarify before blaming each other?
Describe a time a relationship became more honest after an awkward conversation.
What is difficult about letting someone see you before you have worked everything out?
A person who knows your history still needs to learn your present. What has changed about you recently?
How do you decide whose criticism deserves your attention?
Be offered help with a task or permission to leave the task unfinished?
Someone calls your new boundary a lack of trust. How would you separate those ideas?
When have you stayed in a conversation to avoid seeming unkind?
Tell me about an act of repair nobody else noticed but which mattered to you.
A relationship does not become mutual simply because both people have strong feelings. What else makes it mutual?
What have you learnt about yourself from the way you ask for reassurance?
Which relationship taught you to separate gratitude from indebtedness?
Sometimes an old argument continues through new subjects. How do you recognise the older concern underneath?
Someone trusts you with information which changes how you view a mutual acquaintance. How would you protect both privacy and fairness?
What do you find difficult about accepting a thoughtful refusal?
Describe a time someone made room for your uncertainty without deciding for you.
Understand why somebody left or understand why you wanted them to stay?
What do you want to preserve in yourself when a relationship ends badly?
Wanting somebody to improve differs from wanting them to become easier for you. How do you examine your motives?
A person offers practical help after you asked for emotional understanding. How would you explain the difference?
When have you interpreted somebody's limit as a judgement of your worth?
Tell me about a time you let someone care for you in a way unfamiliar to you.
Which truth about your needs took you longest to stop apologising for?
Trust sometimes grows from hearing a clear 'I don't know.' Who has helped you appreciate this?
What do you notice when you feel tempted to test someone's loyalty?
Revisit a painful misunderstanding or accept a respectful relationship without complete agreement about the past?
A person wants a second chance while you need evidence over time. What would you explain about rebuilding confidence?
Describe a relationship in which you learnt to enjoy another person's independence.
When does giving advice help you avoid sitting with somebody's pain?
Being considerate includes letting people make choices you would not make. Which choice has tested this for you?
What has caring for someone through a long illness taught you about asking for help yourself?
Whose approval becomes louder in your mind when you make a personal decision?
A generous person still needs a way to say they have reached their limit. What helps you hear this without taking offence?
Someone remembers your past mistakes more readily than your recent efforts. How would you address the imbalance?
Tell me about a time an unexpected question helped you feel less alone in a relationship.
Hear an uncomfortable concern from someone close or notice they have quietly stopped trying?
Which version of yourself appears when you fear losing someone?
A relationship needs room for ordinary days, not only important conversations. What makes ordinary time feel connected?
What does it mean to be accountable without making yourself the villain in every story?
Somebody accepts your help but rejects your advice. How would you respect the distinction?
Describe a time you recognised another person's effort before it produced a result.
When has your wish to protect someone prevented you from asking what they wanted?
Somebody's absence sometimes reveals how much they quietly contributed. What have you noticed after a person stepped back?
Which conversation would become easier if nobody had to prove who cared more?
Offer someone space to reconsider or ask for an immediate clear answer?
Two people describe the same relationship using different words. What would you want them to compare beyond the labels?
What helps you notice when you are defending your image instead of hearing someone?
Tell me about a person whose honest limits made them more dependable to you.
Forgiveness does not dictate the same future level of access. How have you thought about access after forgiveness?
What do you need in order to hear 'you hurt me' without immediately explaining yourself?
When has asking for less become a way of expecting less disappointment?
A private disappointment sometimes becomes a public joke before anyone addresses it. How do you notice this shift?
Someone asks you to choose a side before you understand the disagreement. What would help you remain fair?
Describe a time you and somebody else found different meanings in a shared experience.
Which relationship changed your understanding of emotional generosity?
Receive an apology with a concrete change or an explanation which helps you understand the mistake?
Taking time to reply does not settle whether someone cares. What evidence do you trust more than speed?
When do you confuse solving somebody's problem with being useful to them?
A person wants you to keep a promise made before your circumstances changed. What should you discuss honestly?
Tell me about a time you respected somebody more after seeing a limitation they acknowledged.
What does your response to being misunderstood reveal about what matters to you?
A relationship sometimes ends long before its routines do. What helps you recognise when routine has replaced connection?
Which expectation do you need to express before it turns into resentment?
Be trusted with someone's uncertainty or with a decision they have already made?
Someone wants to restore a relationship exactly as it was. What would you want to keep different?
Describe a time your understanding of fairness changed after hearing another person's experience.
An honest relationship leaves room for saying, 'I care, and I disagree.' What makes those words hard to hear?
When have you felt closer to someone after admitting a difference you had hidden?
Which expression of care do you struggle to recognise because it differs from your own?
People sometimes offer certainty when companionship is what they have to give. What has helped you feel supported amid uncertainty?
A person says they no longer know where they stand with you. What would you want to clarify first?
Tell me about someone who made it safe for you to correct their impression of you.
Know the limits of somebody's availability or receive unpredictable moments of intense attention?
What makes you hesitate before asking a person close to you for help?
Knowing somebody well does not mean knowing what they need today. When have you had to ask again?
When has accepting somebody's kindness challenged an old belief about yourself?
Someone apologises for having a need before telling you what it is. How would you make the conversation less burdensome?
Describe a time choosing not to reply immediately helped you answer more honestly.
Which form of conflict makes you feel invisible rather than opposed?
A relationship's strongest person sometimes becomes its least consulted person. What makes consultation disappear?
What helps you recognise affection which comes with conditions you cannot accept?
Ask for reassurance about the relationship or ask for clarity about one particular behaviour?
Someone says a boundary surprised them because you never mentioned it before. How would you discuss a newly recognised limit?
Tell me about a time you felt proud of how you treated somebody despite an unresolved disagreement.
Keeping a connection alive requires more than avoiding its ending. What does active care involve for you?
When has another person's trust in you encouraged you to become more honest with yourself?
What are you asking somebody to carry when you say, 'You know what I'm like'?
Silence might mean comfort, fear or exhaustion. What helps you resist guessing its meaning for somebody else?
Two people repeatedly miss each other's attempts to repair a disagreement. What might each need to make clearer?
Describe a relationship where a difficult limit prevented a deeper resentment.
Understand someone's reasons without agreeing or receive agreement without feeling understood?
Which habit of comparison makes it harder to appreciate a particular relationship?
Care feels different when it allows you to remain the author of your choices. When have you experienced this?
When do you expect someone to recognise a need you have never expressed?
A person wants an honest answer but reacts painfully when they hear it. How would you balance truth and care?
Tell me about a time a relationship became less intense and more secure.
What do you want to believe about people even after a disappointment?
Sometimes the hardest part of accepting an apology is giving up an old explanation of the person. Have you experienced this?
Which relationship taught you a difference between being responsible and feeling guilty?
Be asked what support you want or be offered a small, specific form of help?
Somebody's effort improves while your feelings remain uncertain. How would you speak honestly without dismissing their effort?
Describe a time somebody's straightforward answer freed you from guessing.
A person's needs do not become less real because they express them calmly. What do you notice first when somebody asks for help?
When does being understanding begin to silence an important part of your experience?
What does a relationship reveal about how you respond to somebody else's freedom?
We sometimes ask for an explanation when we want a different outcome. How do you recognise which one you are seeking?
Someone asks whether you still trust them after a small disagreement. How would you separate disagreement from the wider relationship?
Tell me about a time you accepted care from a person you usually supported.
Receive steady understanding from one person or broad approval from many people?
Which feeling do you most often disguise as irritation around people close to you?
Repair sometimes begins with naming what both people have been avoiding. What makes naming it feel possible?
When have you mistaken someone else's confidence for a reason to doubt your own needs?
A person wants you to explain a limit to everyone affected by it. How much explanation would feel fair?
Describe a time you became kinder without becoming more available.
What would you like to understand about the relationships you leave unspoken?
Some people feel safest when they are useful. What helps you feel welcome when you have nothing to contribute?
Be remembered accurately by someone or be seen generously despite their incomplete understanding?
You realise a relationship rests on an assumption neither person has checked. What would you ask first?
Tell me about a time you chose a difficult conversation over a reassuring assumption.
Which relationship has helped you stop treating a feeling as a verdict about yourself?
A caring response is sometimes a question which leaves the answer open. Which questions have given you room?
What do you want to do differently the next time someone trusts you with uncertainty?
Somebody wants to know whether their best effort is enough for you. What would an honest answer need to acknowledge?
Describe a moment when you felt free to belong without hiding a difference.
Which part of caring for another person has made you more aware of your own limits?
Two people might agree on what happened and still disagree on what it meant. What helps them keep listening?
Ask what someone intended to preserve or what they feared losing during an argument?
What would greater honesty require you to risk in a relationship you value?
You notice someone has stopped asking you for anything. How would you find out whether they feel independent or discouraged?
Tell me about a time someone let your answer remain complicated.
Respect sometimes means accepting a decision without receiving an explanation you like. Which decisions test this for you?
What helps you remain interested in somebody after you stop agreeing on important things?
Closeness changes when a person no longer has to make their pain persuasive. What makes you feel believed?
When has a relationship asked you to become more patient with ambiguity?
What has a relationship across a large difference in income taught you about dignity?
A former mentor now treats you as an equal, but you still seek permission. What would help you adjust?
Tell me about a connection which survived after the project bringing you together ended.
Which parts of yourself feel easier to share in one language than another with people close to you?
Defending an absent person requires care about accuracy as well as loyalty. When have you had to balance both?
